premise.claim: Dependabot: "Bumps go.uber.org/zap from 1.27.0 to 1.28.0" — routine maintenance bump; release notes claim 1.27.1 fixes (prevent Object from panicking on nils; fix a race condition in WithLazy) and the 1.28.0 PreWriteHook enhancement become available to fluid.
premise.reportedComponent: go.uber.org/zap as vendored into fluid (go.mod, go.sum, vendor/modules.txt, vendor/go.uber.org/zap/**)
premise.patchedComponent: exactly those files — see PR file list (18 files, all zap-bump related)
premise.evidence: The upgrade premise is confirmed as coherent and safe: vendor tree byte-identical to upstream v1.28.0 (results/vendor-fidelity-head.txt), go.sum matches checksum DB, `go mod tidy` yields zero drift, full build passes, and the vendored tree demonstrably carries >=1.27.1 semantics (A3/A4 fail on base, pass on head — results/unit-base.txt vs results/unit-head.txt). This is a maintenance bump, so 'confirmed' means: the claimed upgrade is genuine, complete, and non-regressive, not that a user-facing bug existed on base.

liveNote: No live layer needed: this PR changes no fluid runtime behavior directly (fluid's own zap call sites are AddCaller/NewProductionEncoderConfig/NewDevelopmentEncoderConfig/NewConsoleEncoder/CapitalLevelEncoder/ISO8601TimeEncoder — all untouched upstream). Controller-runtime, the only vendored-graph consumer of the changed zap APIs, uses none of the changed symbols except zapcore.Level (via its own lowercase levelStrings map, unaffected). Per round policy the live/KUBECONFIG layer is skipped.
